scenario: AI 编码面试刚开始，你被放进一个已有多文件项目，类、模型和业务逻辑都已经存在。
scenario_en: At the start of an AI coding interview, you are dropped into an existing multi-file project with classes, models, and business logic already in place.
q: 面对陌生代码库，最先应该做什么？
q_en: What should you do first when facing an unfamiliar codebase?
options: 马上让 AI 根据题目生成完整实现
先重构目录结构，让代码更符合你的习惯
先快速建立代码库地图，再决定怎么提示 AI
只读 README 和文件名，跳过打开源码这一步
why: 已有项目里最容易踩的坑是改到现有模式之外；先扫入口、模型和状态流建地图，提示才会贴合代码库。代价是多花几分钟阅读，但能省下返工。
why_en: Orient yourself first so your prompts fit the entry points, models, and state flow that already exist, instead of drifting from established patterns.
whenOtherWins: 如果是完全空白的开放式题目，可以更快进入建模和实现，但仍要先读清需求边界。
tradeoff: 先建心智地图 vs 直接提示 AI 生成
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Task[New repo] --> Read[Read structure]
  Read --> Map[Mental map]
  Map --> Plan[Plan change]
  Plan --> Prompt[Prompt AI]
options_en: Ask the AI to generate a full implementation right away.
Refactor the directory structure to match your own habits first.
Quickly build a mental map of the codebase, then decide how to prompt the AI.
Only skim the README and file names, and skip opening the source code.

termDefinitions.meaning: 项目根目录下介绍用途和用法的说明文件，内容常滞后于实际代码。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A README is the top-level file that explains a project's purpose, and it often lags behind the actual code.

optionExplanations: 跳过阅读直接让 AI 出完整实现，提示词会撞上你还没发现的既有模式，容易返工。
还没弄懂用途就按个人习惯重排目录，会打乱现有约定，扩大改动范围。
花几分钟扫一遍入口、核心模型和状态怎么流转，后续提示才不会脱离真实代码结构。
README 常年落后于代码，只看它和文件名看不到真实的类和调用关系。
optionExplanations_en: Skipping straight to a full AI-generated implementation means your prompts collide with patterns you haven't discovered yet.
Reordering folders to your own taste before you understand them breaks existing conventions and widens the change.
A few minutes tracing entry points, key models, and how state moves keeps later prompts grounded in what's actually there.
A README usually lags the code, so skimming it and file names alone hides the real classes and call paths.

scenario: 90 分钟 AI 编码面试给你一个 8000 行陌生仓库，前 10 分钟明确留给定向阅读。
scenario_en: In a 90-minute AI-assisted coding interview you get an 8,000-line unfamiliar repo, and the first ten minutes are explicitly set aside for orientation.
q: 跳过代码库阅读、直接提示 AI，最容易给面试官什么信号？
q_en: If you skip codebase reading and prompt the AI right away, what signal are you most likely sending the interviewer?
options: 你会在不了解系统时就开始改代码
证明你效率很高，能更快切入正题开始写代码
你已经掌握了所有业务约束
你不需要验证 AI 输出
why: 面试官会把这种行为映射到真实团队协作：没弄懂系统就动手，后续决策也更容易偏离现有设计。代价是这类信号会直接拉低候选人评价。
why_en: Skipping orientation signals you might change unfamiliar production code before understanding it, which lowers how interviewers rate you.
options_en: You might start changing a system before you understand it.
It proves you're efficient and can jump straight into writing code.
You already grasp all the business constraints.
You don't need to verify AI output.
optionExplanations: 这正是面试官最担心的团队协作风险——没弄懂系统就动手改代码。
面试官不会把跳步骤当成效率高，反而会读成没弄懂系统就动手的风险信号。
几分钟内不可能吃透全部业务约束，这个假设站不住脚。
跳过阅读和跳过验证 AI 输出是两件独立的事，混为一谈答不到点上。
optionExplanations_en: That's exactly the team-collaboration risk interviewers watch for — changing a system before you understand it.
Interviewers don't read skipped steps as efficiency; they read it as the risk of touching code before you understand it.
No one absorbs every business constraint in a few minutes, so this assumption doesn't hold.
Skipping reading and skipping AI-output verification are separate issues; this answer misses the point.

q: 把快速建立代码库心智地图的顺序排好：
q_en: Put the quick codebase orientation steps in order:
steps: 追踪数据如何流过关键类和方法
找到执行入口或请求入口
确认公共接口、状态归属和测试
先看目录结构，判断项目的大致组织方式
why: 先看整体组织，再找入口并顺着数据流深入，最后确认接口、状态和测试，能用最少时间抓住代码库骨架。
why_en: A strong orientation moves from structure to entry point to data flow, then checks interfaces, state ownership, and tests.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Tree[Project tree] --> Entry[Entry points]
  Entry --> Core[Core logic]
  Core --> Data[Data models]
  Data --> Tests[Tests]

scenario: 只剩 10 分钟摸清一个陌生 HTTP 服务怎么处理请求，时间只够读三四个文件。
scenario_en: You have ten minutes to figure out how an unfamiliar HTTP service handles a request, enough time for only three or four files.
q: 阅读陌生项目时，为什么入口点通常是第一批要找的代码？
q_en: When reading an unfamiliar project, why are entry points usually among the first code to find?
options: 入口点里一定包含全部业务逻辑，读完就不用再看别处
入口点通常是全库最短、读起来最快的文件
入口点能够替代阅读测试用例
入口点标出执行起点和请求/命令进入系统的方式
why: 入口点能让你沿真实调用路径追踪对象创建和方法调用，而不是孤立读文件；代价是复杂系统里入口可能不止一个。
why_en: The entry point shows where execution begins so you can trace real calls instead of reading files in isolation.
options_en: The entry point always contains all the business logic, so once you've read it you don't need to look anywhere else.
The entry point is usually the shortest file in the repo, so it's the fastest read.
The entry point can replace reading the test suite.
The entry point marks where execution starts and how requests or commands enter the system.

termDefinitions.meaning: 程序或服务开始执行的位置，比如 main 函数或 HTTP 请求处理器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The entry point is where a program or service begins executing, such as a main function or an HTTP request handler.

optionExplanations: 真实系统的业务逻辑通常散在多个类里，读完入口就收手会让你漏读关键路径。
文件长短和是否值得优先读没有必然关系，入口的价值不在于短。
测试说明预期行为，入口说明调用路径，两者互补，谁都替代不了谁。
顺着入口能看到对象怎么被创建、方法怎么被调用，是最快建立调用图的起点。
optionExplanations_en: Real systems spread logic across many classes, so stopping after the entry file makes you miss the key paths.
File length has no real link to priority; the entry point's value isn't about being short.
Tests describe expected behavior while the entry point traces the call path — neither substitutes for the other.
Following it shows what gets instantiated and which methods get called, the fastest way to sketch the call graph.

scenario: 面试给你一个 200 文件的陌生仓库，限时 10 分钟挑出值得精读的几处。
scenario_en: The interview hands you an unfamiliar 200-file repo and ten minutes to pick the few places worth reading closely.
q: 哪些位置通常是陌生代码库里的高价值“代码指针”？（多选）
q_en: Which places are usually high-value code pointers in an unfamiliar codebase? (Select all that apply.)
options: 请求处理器、main 函数或 CLI 入口
承载核心业务逻辑的复杂函数
核心数据模型和类层级
随机挑一个样式文件从头读到尾
why: 入口、核心函数和数据模型能解释系统怎么启动、做什么、数据长什么样；随机文件通常解锁不了全局理解。
why_en: Entry points, core functions, and data models reveal how the system starts, what it does, and how data is shaped, far more than a random file.
options_en: Request handlers, the main function, or the CLI entry point.
The complex function that carries the core business logic.
Core data models and the class hierarchy.
Pick a random stylesheet file and read it start to end.

termDefinitions.meaning: 通过终端命令与程序交互的入口方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CLI is a command-line interface where you interact with a program via terminal commands.

optionExplanations: 顺着请求处理器或 main/CLI 入口，能看清请求怎么被处理、调用了哪些组件。
读懂承载核心逻辑的那几个复杂函数，比啃十几个简单辅助文件更快建立系统直觉。
看清数据模型和类层级里的对象关系，能提前挡住很多因误解数据形状引发的 bug。
样式文件通常不牵动业务逻辑，从头读到尾也解锁不了对系统行为的理解。
optionExplanations_en: Tracing the request handler or main/CLI entry shows how requests get handled and which components get called.
Reading the few complex functions that carry core logic builds system intuition faster than a dozen small helpers.
Seeing the model relationships and class hierarchy heads off many bugs caused by misreading the data shape.
A stylesheet rarely touches business logic, so reading it end to end won't unlock behavior understanding.

q: 补全入口点阅读目标：
q_en: Complete the goal of reading an entry point:
text: 找到入口点后，要顺着它看清哪些{{类被实例化}}、哪些{{方法被调用}}，以及组件之间如何{{交接工作}}。
why: 入口点的价值不只是“文件在哪”，而是让你沿真实执行路径理解系统组织。
why_en: An entry point matters because it reveals instantiation, method calls, and handoffs along the real execution path.

scenario: 限时读码只剩 5 分钟，要在一个 300 行核心函数和 12 个小辅助文件之间二选一。
scenario_en: With five minutes of reading time left, you must choose between one 300-line core function and twelve small helper files.
q: 相比读十几个简单辅助文件，优先读“硬核心”函数的主要收益是？
q_en: Compared with reading a dozen simple helper files, what is the main benefit of reading the hard core function first?
options: 它写出来就一定不会有 bug，可以直接信任
它通常揭示系统真实的输入输出与业务流程
它能替代你阅读全部数据模型
它通常完全由 AI 自动生成而成
why: 核心函数往往是其他代码围绕的中心；理解它的调用方式、输入和输出，能比读一堆辅助文件更快建立系统直觉。
why_en: The core function often reveals the real inputs, outputs, and workflow that the rest of the code supports.
tradeoff: 读核心函数快速建直觉 vs 读大量辅助文件覆盖细节
options_en: It's written so it's guaranteed not to have bugs, so you can trust it outright.
It usually reveals the system's real inputs, outputs, and business workflow.
It lets you skip reading all the data models.
It is always entirely AI-generated.
optionExplanations: 复杂代码照样可能有 bug，核心函数不提供正确性保证，不能拿来直接信任。
核心函数往往浓缩了系统真正的输入输出和业务流程，是建立直觉的捷径。
数据模型决定输入的形状，读完核心函数后仍要回头确认模型。
代码来源和是否值得优先读没有因果关系，这个理由文不对题。
optionExplanations_en: Complex code can still hide bugs; the core function offers no correctness guarantee to trust blindly.
The core function usually concentrates the real inputs, outputs, and workflow — a shortcut to intuition.
Data models define the input shape, so you still circle back to them after the core function.
How the code was generated has no bearing on whether it's worth reading first.

scenario: 你在游戏项目中看到 `Game` 持有 `Board`，`Board` 里有 `Cell`，每个 `Cell` 记录状态和邻居。
scenario_en: In a game project, `Game` owns a `Board`; the `Board` contains `Cell`s, and each `Cell` tracks state and neighbors.
q: 接下来最有价值的理解重点是什么？
q_en: What is the most valuable thing to understand next?
options: 画清核心对象之间的关系和数据如何流动
先忽略模型，直接让 AI 写搜索算法
把所有类合并成一个文件
只看 UI 渲染代码
why: 数据模型定义了后续逻辑的边界，很多 bug 都来自误解对象关系或数据形状；代价是花几分钟画关系图，换来更少的返工。
why_en: Core object relationships define the boundaries for later logic, and many bugs come from misunderstanding the data shape.
whenOtherWins: 如果项目确实是单函数算法题且没有持久模型，模型映射可以很轻，但仍要确认输入输出结构。
tradeoff: 先画清对象关系 vs 直接跳到算法实现
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Models[Data models] --> State[State shape]
  State --> Invariants[Invariants]
  Invariants --> SafeChange[Safer change]
options_en: Map out how the core objects relate and how data flows between them.
Ignore the model and have the AI write the search algorithm right away.
Merge all the classes into a single file.
Only look at the UI rendering code.
optionExplanations: 先理清 Game/Board/Cell 的持有关系和数据流向，后续提示才能准确描述结构。
AI 不清楚 Cell 的状态和邻居长什么样，跳过模型直接写搜索容易出错。
合并类会抹掉原本的职责边界，让后续改动更难追踪。
UI 代码看不到 Board/Cell 的状态和邻居关系，解决不了这道题的核心。
optionExplanations_en: Mapping how Game, Board, and Cell hold each other and how data flows keeps later prompts accurate.
The AI doesn't know Cell's state and neighbor shape, so skipping the model risks a broken search.
Merging the classes erases the original responsibility boundaries, making future changes harder to trace.
UI code never shows Board or Cell's state and neighbors, so it misses this task's real question.

q: 补全数据模型的常见风险链：
q_en: Complete the common risk chain around data models:
text: 如果误解数据模型，后续 bug 往往来自错误判断数据的{{形状}}、{{归属}}和{{流向}}。
why: 实现逻辑时你会不断依赖这些假设，一开始错了，AI 生成的代码也会跟着错。
why_en: Wrong assumptions about data shape, ownership, and flow propagate into the code the AI generates.

rows: AI 编出不存在的字段
两处各改一半，状态漂移
副作用漏在另一条路径

scenario: 你想在几秒内看完整个项目有哪些文件，用文件名和目录先判断 MVC、分层或按功能模块组织。
scenario_en: You want to see all project files in seconds and use names and folders to infer MVC, layering, or feature-based organization.
q: 先摸清项目文件全貌，该跑哪条命令？
q_en: Which command should you run first to map the project files?
options: npm test
git commit -am orient
find . -type f
rm -rf node_modules
why: 先列出文件树能快速暴露项目组织方式，再决定哪些入口、模型和测试值得深入读；代价是这一步只给结构，不给行为细节。
why_en: Listing files first quickly exposes the project's organization so you can choose which entry points and models to inspect next.
whenOtherWins: 如果环境有更快更清晰的工具，比如 `rg --files` 或 IDE 文件树，也可以用它达到同样目的。
tradeoff: 先看文件全貌 vs 直接打开某个文件深入
codeSample:
find . -type f
# 观察目录和文件名：models/controllers/views、layers、features、tests 等
options_en: Run `npm test`.
Run `git commit -am orient`.
Run `find . -type f` to list every file.
Run `rm -rf node_modules`.

termDefinitions.meaning: Unix 命令，用来按条件递归列出文件系统里的文件和目录。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: find is a Unix command that recursively lists files and directories matching given criteria.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把代码分成模型、视图、控制器三层的经典架构模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MVC is a classic architecture that splits code into Model, View, and Controller layers.

optionExplanations: 跑测试能看到行为基线，但看不到目录结构和文件分布。
还没做任何可解释的改动就提交，和摸清结构完全无关。
几秒内递归列出全部文件名和目录，足够判断项目的组织方式。
删依赖只在修复安装污染时才考虑，对了解结构毫无帮助还有破坏性。
optionExplanations_en: Running the tests shows a behavior baseline, not the directory layout or file distribution.
Committing before making any explainable change has nothing to do with mapping the structure.
Recursively listing every filename and folder in seconds is enough to judge the project's organization.
Deleting dependencies is only for fixing install pollution — it's destructive and reveals nothing about structure.

scenario: 接下来要在陌生 Java 服务里加一个新接口，动手前得先判断新代码放哪一层。
scenario_en: You are about to add a new endpoint to an unfamiliar Java service and must first decide which layer the new code belongs in.
q: 目录结构为什么能帮助你判断后续该怎么改代码？
q_en: Why can directory structure help you decide how to change code later?
options: 文件名能保证代码没有 bug
只要目录清楚，就不需要读方法体
目录越深，设计一定越好
它常暴露 MVC 或分层等架构模式
why: 目录和文件名会提示职责边界，例如数据库访问是否集中在 repository 层，避免新逻辑塞错位置。
why_en: The directory layout often reveals architectural boundaries such as MVC, layers, or feature modules, showing where new code belongs.
options_en: Filenames guarantee the code has no bugs.
As long as folders are clear, you never need to read method bodies.
The deeper the directories, the better the design must be.
It often reveals existing patterns like MVC or layered architecture.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专门集中处理数据库访问的代码层，业务代码通过它读写数据而不直接写 SQL。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A repository layer centralizes database access so business code reads and writes through it instead of writing raw SQL.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把代码分成模型、视图、控制器三层的经典架构模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MVC is a classic architecture that splits code into Model, View, and Controller layers.

optionExplanations: 命名和 bug 数量没有必然关系，这个假设站不住脚。
目录只给出骨架，方法体里的具体逻辑仍然需要读。
目录深浅只是组织习惯，跟设计好坏没有必然关系。
看到 controller/service/repository 这类文件夹名，就能猜出新逻辑该放哪一层。
optionExplanations_en: Naming has no real link to bug count, so this assumption doesn't hold.
Folders only give the skeleton — the logic inside each method body still needs reading.
Depth is just an organizational habit, unrelated to whether the design is good.
Seeing folders like controller/service/repository tells you which layer new logic belongs in.

scenario: 代码库把所有数据库访问都放在 repository 层，AI 建议你在 controller 里直接写 SQL。
scenario_en: The codebase puts all database access in a repository layer, but the AI suggests writing SQL directly in a controller.
q: 面对这个建议，最好的反应是什么？
q_en: What is the best reaction to this suggestion?
options: 接受建议，因为 AI 生成速度快
按现有 repository 模式重定向 AI
删除 repository 层，减少文件数量
先提交代码，之后再讨论
why: 强候选人会让 AI 遵守现有关注点分离，而不是引入和代码库冲突的访问路径；代价是要多打一轮字说明约束，但避免了架构漂移。
why_en: A strong candidate redirects the AI to follow the existing repository pattern instead of scattering direct SQL into the controller.
whenOtherWins: 只有当现有抽象明显无法表达新需求且能解释迁移成本时，才考虑调整架构边界。
tradeoff: 遵守现有 repository 边界 vs 图省事直接写 SQL
options_en: Accept it, because the AI generates code fast.
Redirect the AI to follow the existing repository pattern.
Delete the repository layer to reduce the file count.
Commit the code first and discuss it later.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据库访问逻辑集中在一层，业务代码不直接写 SQL 语句。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The repository pattern centralizes database-access logic so business code never writes raw SQL directly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用来查询和操作关系型数据库的语言。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQL is the language used to query and manipulate relational databases.

optionExplanations: 生成速度快只适合原型草稿，不能凌驾于项目已有的架构约定之上。
把 AI 拉回既有的 repository 边界，能保持数据库访问集中，减少后续维护成本。
删层是重构数据访问层的决定，不该在响应一条建议时顺手做掉。
先斩后奏会让和代码库冲突的代码先合入，讨论应该发生在改动之前。
optionExplanations_en: Fast generation fits a prototype draft, not something that should override the project's own architecture.
Steering the AI back to the existing repository boundary keeps database access centralized and cheaper to maintain.
Removing the layer is a deliberate data-access refactor, not a side effect of answering one suggestion.
Landing the code first lets code that clashes with the repo merge before anyone discusses it.

scenario: 刚 clone 陌生仓库，目前只看得到目录树、还没读任何方法体，就要定改动落点。
scenario_en: You just cloned an unfamiliar repo, you can only see the directory tree with no method bodies read yet, and you must decide where the change lands.
q: 从文件结构中可以快速识别哪些组织模式？（多选）
q_en: Which organization patterns can you quickly identify from file structure? (Select all that apply.)
options: MVC：models、views、controllers 分开
分层架构：展示、业务逻辑、数据访问分离
按功能模块聚合相关文件
所有项目都必须是同一种目录结构
why: 这些模式会告诉你新代码应该放到哪里、依赖该朝哪个方向走；最后一个说法不成立，因为项目组织方式本就多样。
why_en: Recognizing MVC, layered, or feature-based structure tells you where new code belongs and how dependencies should flow.
options_en: MVC: models, views, and controllers live in separate folders.
Layered architecture: presentation, business logic, and data access are split apart.
Feature-based structure: related files are grouped by feature.
Every project must use the exact same directory layout.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把代码分成模型、视图、控制器三层的经典架构模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MVC is a classic architecture that splits code into Model, View, and Controller layers.

optionExplanations: 看到 models/views/controllers 三个文件夹并存，就能先按 MVC 猜请求怎么流转。
看到展示、业务逻辑、数据访问分层，就能先按层归类改动该放哪。
看到同一功能的文件聚在一个模块目录里，就能按模块定位改动范围。
现实里项目组织差异很大，把某一种目录规范当成普遍事实会误导判断。
optionExplanations_en: Seeing models/views/controllers as separate folders lets you first read request flow as MVC.
Seeing presentation, business logic, and data access split into layers tells you which layer a change belongs in.
Seeing files for one feature grouped into a module folder lets you locate the change by module.
Real projects vary widely, so treating one layout as universal will mislead you.

scenario: 要让 AI 给一个陌生的 Order 类加功能，且不能破坏它已有的封装约定。
scenario_en: You need the AI to add a feature to an unfamiliar Order class without breaking its existing encapsulation contract.
q: 为什么要特别扫描关键类的 public 和 private 边界？
q_en: Why should you scan the public and private boundary of key classes?
options: 这样可以绕过封装直接改内部数组
private 字段通常比 public 方法更可靠
能知道 AI 该调用哪些公开方法，别碰内部实现
public/private 对面试没有意义
why: 公共接口是类对外承诺的使用方式，把 AI 指向这些接口能减少破坏封装和碰内部状态的风险；代价是要先花时间把接口读全。
why_en: Public interfaces show how classes are meant to be used, keeping the AI from reaching into internals it shouldn't touch.
tradeoff: 遵守公开接口边界 vs 图方便直接碰内部字段
options_en: So you can bypass encapsulation and edit the internal array directly.
Private fields are usually more reliable than public methods.
So you know which public methods the AI should call instead of touching internals.
Public/private boundaries don't matter for the interview.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把对象内部状态隐藏起来，只通过公开方法暴露该暴露的行为。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encapsulation hides an object's internal state and exposes only the behavior meant to be public.

optionExplanations: 绕过封装会让改动脱离类原本的约束，是这个动作的反面用法。
可靠性取决于实现质量本身，和字段是否私有没有必然关系。
扫清公开方法边界后，能把 AI 限定在安全接口上，不去碰内部状态。
面试官恰恰会通过你是否尊重这条边界，判断你对封装的理解。
optionExplanations_en: Bypassing encapsulation pulls the change outside the class's own constraints — that's the opposite of the point.
Reliability depends on implementation quality, not on whether a field happens to be private.
Mapping the public boundary keeps the AI confined to safe methods instead of reaching into internal state.
This is exactly the signal interviewers use to judge whether you respect encapsulation.

scenario: `Deck` 类已有 `getCards()`，内部 `cards` 数组不是公开接口；AI 生成代码直接访问 `deck.cards`。
scenario_en: The `Deck` class already has `getCards()`, and its internal `cards` array is not a public interface; the AI generated code reads `deck.cards` directly.
q: 该怎么纠正这段 AI 生成的代码？
q_en: How should you correct this AI-generated code?
options: 保留直接访问 deck.cards，因为写法更短更省事
把 `cards` 改成全局变量
删除 `getCards()`
改用 `getCards()`，并说明边界
why: 使用公开方法能尊重封装，也让代码贴合项目原本的对象边界；代价是要多说一句提示词，明确该走哪个接口。
why_en: Use the public method because it preserves encapsulation and matches the class's intended boundary.
whenOtherWins: 如果公开接口确实缺失能力，可以先设计一个小的接口扩展，而不是随手穿透内部字段。
tradeoff: 尊重封装走 getCards() vs 图省事直接读内部数组
options_en: Keep the direct deck.cards access because it's shorter and more convenient to write.
Turn `cards` into a global variable.
Delete `getCards()` entirely.
Switch to `getCards()` and state the boundary.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把对象内部状态隐藏起来，只通过公开方法暴露该暴露的行为。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encapsulation hides an object's internal state and exposes only the behavior meant to be public.

optionExplanations: 省几个字符图省事的短访问会绑死内部结构，Deck 一改内部实现这里就炸。
把私有数组升级成全局状态，反而让任何地方都能随意改它，风险更大。
getCards() 本身没问题，删掉它只会让调用方彻底失去安全访问的方式。
改回类已经暴露的公开方法，封装边界不受影响，未来改内部实现也不连累调用方。
optionExplanations_en: Saving a few keystrokes for a more convenient direct access ties this code to internals — the moment Deck changes shape, it breaks.
Promoting the private array to global state lets it be mutated from anywhere, which is riskier, not safer.
getCards() itself isn't the problem; deleting it just leaves callers with no safe way to read cards.
Switching back to the method the class already exposes keeps the boundary intact, so future internal changes don't ripple out.

q: 补全状态管理阅读目标：
q_en: Complete the goal of reading state management:
text: 读状态管理时，要确认状态存在哪里、如何{{变化}}，以及系统是否有{{单一事实源}}。
why: 状态归属决定副作用在哪里发生，也决定你排查 bug 时应该从哪里开始。
why_en: State ownership tells you where side effects happen and where bugs are likely to hide.

scenario: 陌生仓库里购物车数量同时存在 Cart 对象和 UI 状态两处，你要改数量更新逻辑。
scenario_en: In an unfamiliar repo the cart quantity lives in both the Cart object and the UI state, and you need to change the update logic.
q: 如果同一份状态散落在多个对象里，最需要警惕什么？
q_en: If the same state is scattered across multiple objects, what should you watch for most?
options: 副本可能悄悄不同步，bug 难定位
代码一定运行得更快，多存一份状态没有代价
测试数量会自动减少变少
AI 一定能自动修复同步
why: 多处状态意味着更新顺序和同步规则都要清楚，否则 AI 很容易改一处漏一处；代价是排查这类 bug 通常要跨好几个对象。
why_en: Distributed state requires clear synchronization rules, or the AI may update one copy and silently miss another.
options_en: Copies can drift out of sync, hiding bugs.
The code is guaranteed to run faster, and keeping an extra copy of the state costs nothing.
The number of tests automatically shrinks.
The AI is guaranteed to auto-fix the sync.
optionExplanations: 改了一处漏了另一处，副本就会悄悄不同步，bug 常出现在意想不到的地方。
状态分散本身不影响运行速度，多存一份副本也不是没有代价，把两者挂钩没有依据。
测试数量由风险面和行为面决定，不会因为状态分散就自动变少。
AI 看不到隐藏的同步规则，指望它自动补全只是一厢情愿。
optionExplanations_en: Update one copy and miss another, and the copies quietly drift — bugs then surface somewhere unexpected.
Scattered state by itself has no effect on runtime speed, and an extra copy is not free; linking the two has no basis.
Test count follows risk and behavior surface, not how spread out the state is.
The AI can't see hidden sync rules, so expecting it to patch them automatically is wishful thinking.

scenario: 陌生仓库没有任何文档，只有一套单元测试，你要在 10 分钟内搞清预期行为。
scenario_en: The unfamiliar repo ships no docs, only a unit-test suite, and you need to pin down expected behavior in ten minutes.
q: 为什么已有测试是很好的代码库说明文档？
q_en: Why are existing tests good documentation for a codebase?
options: 测试只对 CI 流水线有用，面试里不用花时间看
测试通常展示系统被期望如何使用和返回什么结果
测试一定覆盖所有边界条件
测试能替代对实现的理解
why: 测试把期望行为具体化，还给你一个验证理解和修改是否破坏现有行为的入口；代价是有些测试可能过时或覆盖不全。
why_en: Existing tests document expected behavior and give you a concrete way to verify your understanding.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Tests[Existing tests] --> Examples[Example behavior]
  Tests --> Boundaries[Edge cases]
  Tests --> Baseline[Current health]
  Baseline --> Change[Safer change]
options_en: Tests are only useful for the CI pipeline, so it's not worth spending interview time on them.
Tests usually show how the system is meant to be used and what it should return.
Tests are guaranteed to cover every edge case.
Tests can substitute for understanding the implementation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每次提交代码后自动运行构建和测试的流程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CI, continuous integration, automatically builds and tests code on every commit.

optionExplanations: 把测试价值局限在 CI 流程里，会让你在面试中错过一份现成的行为说明。
读测试能快速看到预期的输入输出，不用靠猜就能校准理解。
很多项目的测试覆盖并不完整，默认它覆盖全部边界会误导判断。
测试展示的是行为，具体为什么这么实现，还是要回源码确认。
optionExplanations_en: Limiting a test's value to the CI pipeline means missing a ready-made behavior spec during the interview.
Reading tests quickly shows the expected input and output without guessing.
Many projects have incomplete coverage, so assuming every edge case is tested will mislead you.
Tests show behavior, but the source is still where you confirm why it's implemented that way.

scenario: 面试第一步先跑测试，你还没改过任何代码，就已经有 3 个测试是红的。
scenario_en: Your first move in the interview is running the test suite, and before you have changed a single line three tests are already red.
q: 刚进项目时运行已有测试，如果测试已经失败，最合理的解读是？
q_en: When you run existing tests at project entry and they already fail, what is the most reasonable interpretation?
options: 一定是你的新代码造成的
应该直接删除失败测试，让流水线先变绿
可能就是题目要你修的已知问题
说明测试完全没有价值
why: 进入前就失败的测试是重要上下文，可能指向 bug 修复阶段的目标或环境问题；代价是要先花时间核实失败原因，别急着下结论。
why_en: Pre-existing failing tests are context you should account for; they might be the very bug you are expected to fix.
options_en: It must have been caused by your new code.
You should delete the failing tests right away so the pipeline turns green.
It could be the exact pre-existing issue you're asked to fix.
It means tests have no value at all.
optionExplanations: 你还没改任何代码，把锅甩给新代码在时间线上根本说不通。
为了让流水线变绿就删掉失败测试，会丢掉一条关于预期行为的重要线索。
先把它当成既有上下文纳入判断，能避免之后重复发现同一个问题。
多数测试仍然通过，个别失败推翻不了测试整体的价值。
optionExplanations_en: You haven't changed anything yet, so blaming new code doesn't hold up on the timeline.
Deleting the failing tests just to turn the pipeline green throws away a real clue about expected behavior.
Treating it as existing context up front avoids rediscovering the same known issue later.
Most tests still pass, so one failure doesn't erase the value of the rest.

scenario: 环境允许断点调试，你还不确定真实运行时对象长什么样。
scenario_en: The environment supports breakpoint debugging, and you still are not sure what the runtime objects really look like.
q: 为什么早一点打开 debugger 有价值？
q_en: Why is it valuable to open the debugger early?
options: 它能自动替你写完所有代码，不用再看源码
它会隐藏所有类型错误
它能替代和面试官沟通
更快看到真实数据形状和执行路径
why: 断点能让你直接观察运行时数据和调用路径，快速校准从阅读中形成的假设；代价是要花时间设好断点和触发条件。
why_en: A debugger quickly shows real runtime data shapes and execution paths, validating what you inferred from reading.
whenOtherWins: 如果环境不支持调试或时间极紧，日志、测试和小规模运行也能提供类似证据。
tradeoff: 断点观察真实运行时 vs 纯靠阅读推断
options_en: It automatically finishes writing all the code for you, so you don't need to look at the source.
It hides every type error.
It replaces talking with the interviewer.
It shows real data shapes and execution paths faster than reading cold.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让程序暂停、单步执行并查看变量和调用栈的开发工具。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A debugger is a tool that pauses code, steps through execution, and inspects variables and the call stack.

termDefinitions.meaning: 调试器里设置的暂停点，程序运行到这里会停下，方便查看当时的变量和调用栈。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A breakpoint is a pause point set in a debugger where execution stops so you can inspect variables and the call stack.

optionExplanations: debugger 不生成代码，指望它写完实现让你不用看源码只会落空。
调试器只是暂停执行方便观察，并不会隐藏类型错误。
叙述思路是讲给面试官听的，调试是用来观察运行时的，两件事不能互相替代。
对象形状不确定时，在断点处直接看真实值比纯靠阅读推断快得多。
optionExplanations_en: The debugger doesn't write code, so expecting it to finish the implementation for you won't pan out.
A debugger just pauses execution so you can look — it doesn't hide type errors.
Narrating your thinking is for the interviewer; debugging is for observing runtime state — the two don't substitute for each other.
When an object's shape is unclear, seeing real values at a breakpoint beats inferring from reading alone.

scenario: 你在读码阶段，已知后面还有扩展和性能阶段，想提前把追问点找出来。
scenario_en: You are in the reading phase, you know scaling and performance phases come later, and you want to spot the follow-up questions in advance.
q: 哪些线索可能暴露后续阶段会追问的约束？（多选）
q_en: Which clues may reveal constraints that later phases will ask about? (Select all that apply.)
options: 注释里写着“只适合 10,000 以内输入”
配置里出现性能限制或开关
README 描述了已知限制
变量名很短
why: 注释、配置和文档里的限制常常预示扩展阶段的问题；变量名长度通常不是约束线索，只是命名风格。
why_en: Comments, config, and docs often reveal constraints that later phases may stress-test.
options_en: A comment says "only works for inputs up to 10,000".
The config exposes a performance limit or feature flag.
The README documents a known limitation.
Variable names are short.
optionExplanations: 看到这条注释就该有心理准备：后续阶段很可能要求处理更大规模。
配置里的性能开关往往正对着后面阶段要改的那个瓶颈。
README 里写的限制条款，经常就是接下来会被追问的那个点。
变量名长短只是命名风格，和系统的规模或性能约束没有实际关联。
optionExplanations_en: Seeing this comment is a heads-up that a later phase will likely ask you to handle a larger scale.
A performance flag in the config often points straight at the bottleneck a later phase targets.
A limitation written in the README is often exactly what gets asked about next.
Variable-name length is just a naming habit, with no real link to scale or performance constraints.

scenario: 你想用 AI 加速理解，但又不想脱离源码、只在聊天窗口里看摘要。
scenario_en: You want to use AI to speed up understanding, but you do not want to leave the source code and read only a chat summary.
q: 怎么用 AI 加速理解又不脱离源码？
q_en: How can you use AI to speed understanding without leaving the source?
options: 让 AI 直接实现所有功能，自己不用再看代码
让 AI 给类和方法加注释，边读代码边核对
只问 AI 最终答案，不读任何文件
把全部文件粘到聊天里等待总结
why: 内联注释让你留在代码里阅读，同时借助 AI 的解释加速建立模型；代价是要先花一轮时间生成注释再确认真假。
why_en: Inline AI-generated comments keep you reading in the code while its explanations speed up your mental model.
whenOtherWins: 如果只需要确认一个很小的概念，直接问一个针对性问题会比批量注释更快。
tradeoff: 留在代码里读注释 vs 只在聊天窗口看摘要
diagram:
flowchart LR
  AskAI[Ask AI to summarize] --> Check[Check in code]
  Check --> Keep[Keep true facts]
  Check --> Reject[Reject hallucinations]
options_en: Have the AI implement every feature directly, so you never have to look at the code yourself.
Have the AI comment each class and method, then read and check them in the code.
Only ask the AI for the final answer without opening any files.
Paste every file into the chat and wait for a summary.
optionExplanations: 把实现整段交给 AI、自己不看代码也不参与理解，容易直接撞上未知的既有模式。
注释和源码同屏，一边读一边核对，理解和验证能同步进行。
只要结论、不读源码，出了错也没有依据去发现。
整份粘贴等总结会丢掉细节，复杂项目最后还是得回源码核对关键路径。
optionExplanations_en: Handing the whole implementation to the AI without ever looking at the code risks colliding with patterns you haven't found.
With comments sitting next to the code, reading and verifying happen at the same time.
Taking only the conclusion without reading the source leaves you no way to catch it if it's wrong.
Pasting everything for a summary loses detail — complex projects still send you back to the source for key paths.

scenario: 你已经找到 `GameBoard` 和 API handler，想让 AI 帮你确认职责和数据流，而不是泛泛总结整个项目。
scenario_en: You have already found `GameBoard` and an API handler, and you want AI to confirm responsibilities and data flow rather than summarize the whole project vaguely.
q: 哪种提示最可能得到有用的取向信息？
q_en: Which prompt is most likely to return useful orientation information?
options: 点名类和数据流的具体提问
笼统提问：“解释这个项目”
让 AI 直接重写全部代码
笼统要求：“随便优化一下”
why: 具体类名和数据流问题会把 AI 限定在你正在读的代码上，输出更容易验证；代价是要先花时间点出准确的类名和路径。
why_en: Naming specific classes and asking about data flow constrains the AI to code you can actually verify.
whenOtherWins: 刚进入完全未知项目时，可以先要一个很短的全局概览，但马上要落回具体文件和类。
tradeoff: 点名类和数据流提问 vs 笼统问“解释项目”
codeSample:
请基于当前代码回答：
1. GameBoard 类的职责是什么？
2. 请求从 API handler 到数据库的主要数据流是什么？
3. 哪些方法有副作用？
options_en: A targeted question naming the class and data flow.
A vague ask: "explain this project."
Ask the AI to rewrite all the code from scratch.
A vague ask: "optimize it a bit."

termDefinitions.meaning: 供程序调用的接口，这里指处理请求的 API handler。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API is an interface programs call; here it refers to the API handler that processes requests.

termDefinitions.meaning: 示例项目里代表游戏棋盘的类名，用作提示词里的具体锚点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GameBoard is the example project's board class, used as a concrete anchor in the prompt.

optionExplanations: 点出 GameBoard 和数据流这些真实名字，答案才能直接对照代码核实。
没有锚点的整体性提问，AI 只能给出泛泛总结，难以核对。
重写全部代码远超取向阶段的需要，改动范围和风险都被放大了。
“优化一下”没有目标指标，AI 的改动方向完全不可控。
optionExplanations_en: Naming real anchors like GameBoard and the data flow keeps the answer checkable against the code.
A question with no concrete anchor only gets a generic summary that's hard to verify.
Rewriting all the code goes far beyond what orientation needs, widening both scope and risk.
"Optimize it" has no target metric, so the AI's direction is uncontrolled.

scenario: AI 说某个方法“返回最短路径”，但你读代码后发现它实际上返回的是所有路径。
scenario_en: The AI says a method "returns the shortest path," but after reading the code you find it actually returns all paths.
q: 这时最重要的动作是什么？
q_en: What is the most important action now?
options: 相信 AI 摘要，因为总结得更快
忽略这处差异，先把功能写完
以源码为准，纠正对方法行为的理解
直接删掉这个被误读的方法
why: AI 的解释只是起点，源码才是事实；不纠正这个误读，后续实现会建立在错误假设上。代价是要多花一步核对，但省下返工。
why_en: AI explanations are only a starting point; the source code is the ground truth you must build on.
options_en: Trust the AI summary because it's faster.
Ignore the discrepancy and finish the feature first.
Trust the source code and correct your understanding of the method.
Just delete the misread method.
optionExplanations: AI 的解释只是起点，把它当成比源码更可信的事实会带偏后续实现。
差异一旦被搁置，就会埋进后续代码里，之后排查的成本更高。
先按源码纠正理解再动手，能避免整段实现建立在错误假设上。
方法本身没有问题，问题出在理解上，删掉方法解决不了这个误读。
optionExplanations_en: The AI's explanation is only a starting point; trusting it over the source will skew what you build next.
Setting the discrepancy aside lets it get buried in later code, raising the cost to debug.
Correcting your understanding from the source first keeps the implementation from resting on a wrong assumption.
The method itself is fine — the problem is the misread, and deleting the method doesn't fix that.

scenario: 代码库使用你不熟悉的 decorators、generics 或框架惯用法，你卡住了两分钟。
scenario_en: The codebase uses unfamiliar decorators, generics, or framework idioms, and you have been stuck for two minutes.
q: 合理的 AI 用法是什么？
q_en: What is a reasonable way to use AI here?
options: 假装看懂，继续提示实现
要求 AI 把所有陌生语法删掉，换成自己熟悉的写法
跳过看不懂的相关文件
让 AI 解释这段语法，再回源码核对
why: 面试官更愿意看到你用 AI 快速补齐语法认知，而不是在不懂的地方硬猜；代价是要花几十秒确认解释是否准确。
why_en: Interviewers would rather see you use AI to quickly close a syntax gap than guess or stall in silence.
whenOtherWins: 如果陌生语法不在当前变更路径上，可以先标记略过，避免被旁支细节拖走。
tradeoff: 用 AI 补齐语法认知 vs 装懂硬猜或跳过
options_en: Pretend to understand and keep prompting for the implementation.
Ask the AI to delete all the unfamiliar syntax and replace it with something you already know.
Skip the files you don't understand.
Ask the AI to explain the syntax, then verify it against the source.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给类或方法附加额外行为的一种语法标记，常见于 Python、TypeScript 等语言。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A decorator is syntax that attaches extra behavior to a class or method, common in languages like Python and TypeScript.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让类型作为参数传入的语言特性，用来写可复用的类型安全代码。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Generics let a type be passed in as a parameter, enabling reusable, type-safe code.

optionExplanations: 带着错误理解继续往下提示，后面的实现只会更容易出错。
陌生语法往往是框架要求的写法，删掉换成自己熟悉的写法可能直接破坏程序。
被跳过的文件很可能正好是本题要改的关键路径。
先问 AI 把语法讲清楚，再回源码核对是否讲对了，几十秒就能补齐认知缺口。
optionExplanations_en: Continuing to prompt on a wrong understanding only makes the implementation more error-prone later.
Unfamiliar syntax is often exactly what the framework requires, so replacing it with something familiar can break the program.
The file you skip past might be precisely the key path this task needs changed.
Asking the AI to explain the syntax, then checking it against the source, closes the gap in seconds.

scenario: 面试刚开始你感到时钟压力，很想马上开始生成代码。
scenario_en: At the start of the interview, you feel time pressure and want to start generating code immediately.
q: 最好的沟通方式是什么？
q_en: What is the best way to communicate?
options: 说明在确认理解代码库，并边读边叙述发现
沉默地读五分钟，不向面试官说明自己在看什么
先让 AI 生成，出错再回头查
直接说不需要看代码
why: 短暂取向是合理的，但要边读边叙述让面试官听到你在形成有效模型；代价是要多说几句，但换来的是面试官的信任。
why_en: Orienting briefly is expected, but narrating what you find keeps the interviewer confident you're building a real model.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官明确要求立刻修一个极小 bug，可以先定位那条路径，同时保持最小必要取向。
tradeoff: 边读边叙述 vs 沉默阅读或跳过取向
options_en: Say you're confirming your understanding first, and narrate findings as you read.
Read silently for five minutes without telling the interviewer what you're looking at.
Let the AI generate code first and debug whatever errors show up.
Tell the interviewer you don't need to look at the code.
optionExplanations: 边读边把发现说出来，面试官能听到你在建立一个真实可靠的模型。
不说出来面试官只看到停滞，猜不到这段沉默里你到底在做什么。
等报错才回头查，付出的时间往往比先取向清楚更多。
这句话在已有项目场景里本身就会被读成一个风险信号。
optionExplanations_en: Narrating findings while you read lets the interviewer hear you building a real, reliable model.
Without narration the interviewer just sees a stall and has no way to tell what that silence is doing.
Waiting for an error to send you back usually costs more time than orienting up front would have.
In an existing-project interview, that line itself reads as a risk signal.

q: 补全有效取向叙述：
q_en: Complete an effective orientation narration:
text: 取向时要说出你正在学到的具体结构，例如“Board 使用 {{二维网格}} 的 Cell，每个 Cell 跟踪自己的{{状态}}和{{邻居}}。”
why: 具体观察让取向阶段显得有产出，也让面试官相信你会基于真实结构做决策。
why_en: Concrete narration makes orientation productive and shows your decisions are grounded in the code.

scenario: 你把一句需求直接丢给 AI，没贴任何真实类名和接口，就让它改这个陌生仓库。
scenario_en: You hand the AI a one-line requirement with no real class names or interfaces attached and let it edit the unfamiliar repo.
q: 如果你假设 AI 已经理解整个代码库，可能出现哪些问题？（多选）
q_en: If you assume the AI already understands the whole codebase, what problems may happen? (Select all that apply.)
options: AI 调用不存在或不该用的接口
AI 复用和项目模式冲突的抽象
AI 忽略关键副作用
AI 自动获得面试官的隐含偏好
why: AI 常缺少完整上下文，你需要把真实类名、接口和约束放进提示，并检查输出有没有偏离；最后一项不成立，偏好不会被自动感知。
why_en: Because the AI may lack full codebase context, you must supply real interfaces and constraints and check its output for drift.
options_en: The AI calls interfaces that don't exist or shouldn't be used.
The AI reuses abstractions that conflict with the project's patterns.
The AI overlooks important side effects.
The AI automatically picks up the interviewer's unstated preferences.

termDefinitions.meaning: 程序对外暴露、供调用的接口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API is the interface a program exposes for other code to call.

optionExplanations: AI 不知道真实接口时，最容易编出听起来合理但项目里根本没有的调用。
项目已有强模式时，AI 习惯性套用的通用抽象最容易和它冲突。
副作用常藏在状态更新或 I/O 里，AI 看不到就容易漏掉，之后在别处炸出来。
面试官的偏好要靠对方说出来，代码库本身不会把它传给 AI。
optionExplanations_en: When the AI lacks real interfaces, it most often invents calls that sound plausible but don't exist.
Where the project has strong existing patterns, the AI's generic abstractions clash with them most.
Side effects often hide in state updates or I/O, so the AI misses them and they surface elsewhere later.
Interviewer preferences must be stated out loud; the codebase itself never passes them to the AI.

scenario: 90 分钟的 AI 编码面试，你感到时钟压力很想立刻开工，但打算先花 5-10 分钟读代码再提示 AI。
scenario_en: In a 90-minute AI coding interview you feel clock pressure and want to start immediately, but you plan to read for five to ten minutes before prompting the AI.
q: 先花 5-10 分钟读代码再提示，这笔时间靠什么回本？
q_en: How does spending five to ten minutes reading first pay for itself?
options: 实现时提示能点名真实类和方法，省的返工多过读的几分钟
读得越久越好，把仓库每个文件都读透 AI 生成才不会出错
读代码本身就是面试的主要评分项，跟后面实现效率无关
面试规则明确规定前十分钟内不许提示 AI 生成代码
why: 5-10 分钟是经验配额不是推导结果：够抓入口、模型和状态骨架，让实现提示点名真实类和方法。代价是这几分钟在时钟压力下感觉没产出，但省下的返工更多。
why_en: Five to ten minutes is a rule-of-thumb budget: enough to grab the entry points, models, and state so implementation prompts can name real classes, not vague descriptions.
whenOtherWins: 如果是完全从零的开放式题目，没有既有代码要摸，取向可以压到最短，直接进入建模和实现。
tradeoff: 花 5-10 分钟建地图 vs 立刻开始提示 AI
options_en: Implementation prompts can name real classes and methods, so saved rework outweighs the few minutes read.
The longer you read the better; only after reading every file will the AI generate without errors.
Reading code is itself the main thing being scored, unrelated to later implementation efficiency.
Interview rules explicitly forbid prompting the AI to generate code in the first ten minutes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 动手改代码前先快速读懂陌生项目结构、模型和状态的过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Orientation is quickly reading an unfamiliar project's structure, models, and state before changing any code.

optionExplanations: 先建地图，实现时提示能直接引用真实类名和方法，AI 少走弯路，省的返工超过这几分钟。
过度取向：读透每个文件会吃掉实现时间，5-10 分钟抓住骨架就该动手了。
取向是为了实现更准，不是单独刷分；当成无关评分项就会忽略真正收益。
并没有这种硬性规则；不读的代价是信号差和返工，不是违规。
optionExplanations_en: Map first and implementation prompts reference real class names and methods, so the AI wanders less and rework saved beats the minutes spent.
Over-orienting: reading every file eats implementation time — five to ten minutes to grab the skeleton is enough before you start.
Orientation exists to make implementation accurate, not to score on its own; treating it as unrelated hides the real payoff.
There is no such hard rule; the cost of not reading is a weak signal and rework, not a violation.

scenario: 你跳过取向，直接让 AI 写一个“给定坐标返回相邻格子”的函数；仓库里其实已有 `BoardUtils.neighbors()` 做同样的事。
scenario_en: You skip orientation and ask the AI to write a function that returns neighboring cells for a coordinate; the repo already has `BoardUtils.neighbors()` doing exactly that.
q: 没先摸清代码库、漏掉这个已有 helper，最直接的代价是什么？
q_en: Having skipped orientation and missed this existing helper, what is the most direct cost?
options: AI 重造一份相同逻辑，仓库里出现两处 neighbors，改一处会漏掉另一处
编译器会报“重复定义”错误，把这份重复实现直接挡在你合入之前
AI 会自动扫描整个仓库，发现并复用那个已有的 neighbors helper
新写的实现更贴合当前需求，通常一定比旧 helper 跑得更快
why: 漏掉已有 helper，AI 会另写一份同义逻辑，仓库里就有了两个事实源；修好一处，另一处仍带旧 bug。代价是重复代码要评审揪出，分叉还会再生 bug。
why_en: Miss the existing helper and the AI writes a second copy of the same logic, so the repo now has two sources of truth; fix a bug in one and the other still carries it.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Skip[Skip orientation] --> Miss[Miss existing helper]
  Miss --> Dup[AI writes duplicate]
  Dup --> Drift[Two sources drift]
  Drift --> Bug[Fix one, other still buggy]
options_en: The AI rebuilds the same logic, so the repo has two neighbors implementations, and fixing one misses the other.
The compiler raises a "duplicate definition" error and blocks the duplicate before you can merge it.
The AI automatically scans the whole repo, finds the existing neighbors helper, and reuses it.
The freshly written implementation fits the current need better and is guaranteed to run faster than the old helper.

termDefinitions.meaning: 封装可复用小功能的工具类或函数，让多处调用共享同一份实现，避免重复造轮子。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A helper class or function packages a small reusable piece of logic so multiple call sites share one implementation.

optionExplanations: 没发现已有 helper，AI 照需求另写一份；两处同义逻辑并存，改一处漏另一处会分叉出 bug。
重名才会报重复定义；新函数换个名字照样编译通过，这正是它隐蔽的地方。
AI 没有全仓上下文，不会主动发现 helper；你不指它，它就当作不存在。
新写的代码没被验证过，也没理由天生更快；这是想当然的假设。
optionExplanations_en: Missing the existing helper, the AI writes a fresh copy; two same-meaning implementations coexist, and fixing one leaves the other to drift into bugs.
A duplicate-definition error needs the same name; the new function under a different name compiles fine — that is what makes it insidious.
The AI has no whole-repo context and won't discover the helper on its own; if you don't point at it, it treats it as nonexistent.
The freshly written code is unverified and has no inherent reason to be faster; this is a wishful assumption.
